summary: AE/SE walkthrough of Redwood Console tracing, request logs, and error analysis. Customer cares most about production debugging, PII handling in logs, and integration with their PagerDuty/SLOs. Agreed to run a small log export and benchmark, send security docs, and schedule POC scoping.
transcript:
[00:00] Priya Malhotra: Hey everyone good afternoon, thanks for carving out time. I'm Priya, AE on the account at Redwood, and with me is Ethan from our SE team and Lina from CS. Who do we have on from BeaconHealth?
[00:08] Marcus Lee: Marcus here, CTO. Anika is on as well and Jon from SRE. Hey.
[00:11] Anika Patel: Hi all.
[00:13] Priya Malhotra: Awesome. Objective today is a focused console walkthrough — specifically tracing, error analysis, and request logs — so you can see how we'd debug production flows. We'll leave Q&A and then outline next steps.
[00:22] Ethan Zhou: Quick note, I'll show live UI, and also a short demo of request-log export and how we attach top-k traces to failed requests.
[00:27] Jon Rivera: Great, we mostly care about root cause — why a particular generate call spiked latency — and how much PII could be in logs.
[00:32] Priya Malhotra: Perfect. I'll hand to Ethan.
[00:34] Ethan Zhou: Cool. Pulling up the Console — bear with me, sometimes the screen share resizes. Ok so this is the Requests view — you can filter by model, route, and timeframe.
[00:45] [00:45] Ethan Zhou: You see here request IDs on the left, status column, tokens consumed, and a small latency sparkline. We also have a column for "trace score" which indicates anomalous internal events.
[00:58] Anika Patel: That "trace score" — is that an actual statistical anomaly or heuristics?
[01:03] Ethan Zhou: It's heuristics + recent baseline. We run a rolling window of per-route medians and flag deviations beyond configurable thresholds. There is an API to pull raw metrics if you want to plug into your own alerting.
[01:15] Marcus Lee: How granular are the traces? We want per-shard, GPU-level timing if possible.
[01:20] Ethan Zhou: Good question. Traces are hierarchical. We capture request->model-inference->kernel stages. For Dedicated and Private installs we can surface device-level timings — e.g., GPU copy, kernel invocation — but in Hosted we give aggregated node-level times and key stage durations. Sometimes the product name gets scrambled in the transcript — uh, sorry — I mean we surface the important spans.
[01:39] Jon Rivera: And KV cache hits? Can I see cache hit ratio per request?
[01:42] Ethan Zhou: Yes, we annotate spans with KV cache metadata — hit, miss, partial hit — and you can filter by that. That shows up in the span details pane.
[01:48] [01:48] Ethan Zhou: Example: here is a request that had a 95% token increase and we can see a spike in model-generation span because KV cache was a miss.
[01:55] Anika Patel: Hmm, can we mask prompt text? We can't have raw PHI in the console.
[02:00] Priya Malhotra: Important point — we offer PII redaction at ingest and masking in the UI. For Hosted we can redact at collection time per-route; for Private you can enforce no prompt text collection or use customer-side redaction before sending.
[02:11] Marcus Lee: What's the retention on request logs by default?
[02:14] Lina Ortega: Default retention is 30 days for hosted by tier, but we have enterprise options to increase retention and export to your S3 or your SIEM.
[02:22] Marcus Lee: Export — what's the format?
[02:24] Ethan Zhou: Exports are JSONL with per-request metadata + span arrays. We can also stream to your Kinesis or put to S3 with encryption via your KMS.
[02:33] Jon Rivera: If we want to run an offline analysis, can we request a subset? Like all 5xxs for a given route in a timeframe?
[02:39] Ethan Zhou: Yep. Filters support status codes, route, model, latency thresholds, KV cache tags, any metadata tag. You can export filtered results or run an ad-hoc query in Console and then export.
[02:47] [02:47] Marcus Lee: Walk me through a failure example — we've had a case where latency randomly jumps from 80ms to 3s.
[02:53] Ethan Zhou: Sure — here's an example trace. At 00:00 request enters. The pre-proc span shows 20ms, model-infer shows 2.9s. Looking into the kernel-level annotations we see a GPU memory copy stall and then a fallback to CPU quantized path — so a model cold-start or memory pressure event. In Dedicated this would be surfaced as device OOM hints.
[03:14] Anika Patel: How do you detect fallback to different model variants?
[03:18] Ethan Zhou: We attach a "served-with" tag to request metadata — e.g., redwood/llama-2-q8_64 — and if a fallback occurs we show the fallback chain and reason.
[03:26] Marcus Lee: You mentioned canary and fallback policies earlier — can the console show rollout state?
[03:30] Priya Malhotra: Yes, Rollouts view shows percentage traffic, models in the pool, and automatic fallback logs. For example, if latency breaches SLO on a canary, the system can auto-failover to the stable variant and we log that as an event with request IDs.
[03:43] Jon Rivera: Ok. On SSO and auditing — we need per-request audit logs forwarding to Splunk.
[03:48] Lina Ortega: We support audit log forwarding, SAML-based SSO, RBAC and granular token-level audit. The audit logs are separate from request logs and are forwarded in real-time.
[03:58] Anika Patel: Do audit logs include the prompt?
[04:00] Priya Malhotra: By default audit logs include metadata about actions (who pulled export, who changed rollout) but not prompt content unless you enable deeper logging. For compliance we can turn off prompt capture.
[04:10] [04:10] Marcus Lee: How about encryption at rest and in transit? We use customer-managed KMS for keys in private deployments.
[04:16] Ethan Zhou: In Hosted we manage keys but we support BYOK for Dedicated and Private. All transfers use TLS and S3 exports can be encrypted with your KMS prefix.
[04:25] Jon Rivera: Great. Let's talk about sampling — we can't keep full logs for 100% of traffic.
[04:29] Ethan Zhou: Absolutely. We have adaptive sampling policies: deterministic sampling (e.g., 1% of requests), error-triggered sampling (capture all 5xx and 4xx above X ms), and stratified sampling by route. You can configure per-route sampling and we persist the sampling decision in headers for correlation.
[04:44] Anika Patel: Does adaptive sampling break debugging of rare errors?
[04:47] Ethan Zhou: We recommend error-triggered capture so you always capture a representative set of failures. You can temporarily override sampling for a route during an incident.
[04:55] [04:55] Marcus Lee: On the traces, sometimes we have batch requests that fan out — can I see correlation across sub-requests?
[05:00] Ethan Zhou: Yes, we maintain trace parent-child IDs and present them in a flamechart. For batched fan-outs you can collapse or expand spans and view combined latency vs per-subreq.
[05:09] Priya Malhotra: Quick note: some transcriptions may show product names slightly off, for instance "Rudwood" instead of Redwood — ignore that, sorry.
[05:17] Anika Patel: (laughs) got it.
[05:19] [05:19] Jon Rivera: Can we create alerts from the Console based on trace-level conditions?
[05:22] Ethan Zhou: Yes, alerting rules can be set on aggregated metrics or on trace conditions like repeated 'GPU copy stall' events, error rate per route, or tail latency percentiles. Alerts can notify Slack, PagerDuty, or webhooks.
[05:33] Marcus Lee: Do you keep a mapping between request IDs and downstream tool logs? We use Heka/Fluentd and want to correlate.
[05:39] Ethan Zhou: We support correlation IDs — you can inject your trace-id into request metadata and our export preserves it. We also can push logs to your syslog and provide a mapping table.
[05:47] Anika Patel: Let's talk about a real integration scenario: we want an on-call flow where SRE sees the trace, then clicks a CTA to open a PagerDuty incident with pre-populated context.
[05:56] Ethan Zhou: That's supported. There's an "Open Incident" action that creates a PagerDuty incident with link to the trace and attaches the top 5 traces as JSON. You can also set runbooks or internal notes.
[06:05] [06:05] Marcus Lee: Okay would love to see a quick example of exporting error traces to S3.
[06:09] Ethan Zhou: I'll trigger a filter for status:5xx, last 2 hours, route: /summarize. Running export... and sending to the configured S3 bucket — job queued. In this demo I've used a sandbox bucket; for production we'd wire to your account.
[06:25] Anika Patel: You said job queued — how long does it take?
[06:28] Ethan Zhou: Depends on volume; for a couple of thousand records typically under a minute. For a large export we chunk and compress.
[06:35] Jon Rivera: Any throttling concerns?
[06:37] Ethan Zhou: Exports are rate-limited per account, but you can request higher quotas for POC. Also we support incremental exports.
[06:44] [06:44] Anika Patel: Can we get the exported payload schema before we wire the consumer?
[06:48] Priya Malhotra: Yes — Ethan will drop a schema doc along with the sample export and a small script to map fields into your ELK.
[06:55] Ethan Zhou: On error analysis, Console surfaces top-N stack traces and groups by root cause using a similarity heuristic. It's not perfect — sometimes semantically different errors are grouped — but we provide filters to re-cluster.
[07:07] Marcus Lee: Similarity heuristic — is that ML based?
[07:10] Ethan Zhou: It's a hybrid: token-based fingerprinting plus some ML features for fuzzy matching. You can tune sensitivity.
[07:17] [07:17] Anika Patel: Let's talk about the Optimize recommendations — this is slightly adjacent but useful.
[07:21] Priya Malhotra: Redwood Optimize will recommend batching and quantization profiles by route. The Console surfaces potential token savings and projected cost delta if you switch to q4_0 or to a smaller model variant.
[07:33] Marcus Lee: How accurate are those cost projections?
[07:35] Ethan Zhou: They use historical per-token distributions, request sizes, and our kernel throughput models. Typically within 5-10% of observed cost after rollout, though will vary with traffic changes.
[07:45] Jon Rivera: For an internal POC we'll likely try Dedicated or Private — will tracing differ?
[07:50] Ethan Zhou: In Dedicated and Private you get more granular device-level traces and more control over retention and encryption. The console UI is the same; only the backend telemetry granularity changes.
[08:01] Anika Patel: Are there any limitations when using Private in an air-gapped environment?
[08:05] Priya Malhotra: In air-gapped on-prem deployments we ship a collector that runs internally and writes to your internal object store. You still get the Console control plane if it's VPC-connected; fully air-gapped installs have a local Console bundle. We can share topology guides.
[08:18] [08:18] Marcus Lee: Security: does Eks or GKE integration affect trace collection? We run on GKE.
[08:22] Ethan Zhou: We provide a sidecar collector or daemonset that extracts telemetry before it leaves your cluster. For GKE/EKS we have Kubernetes integration docs.
[08:30] Anika Patel: If we want to disable prompt capture globally, but enable it for a single route temporarily, is that straightforward?
[08:35] Ethan Zhou: Yes — per-route telemetry flags allow you to override default collection settings. You can also set a time-based override.
[08:42] [08:42] Jon Rivera: Let's talk cost implications of verbose tracing — how much does it add?
[08:46] Ethan Zhou: Depends on sampling and retention. Full payload capture at high volume can add storage and egress costs; Optimize will estimate this and suggest sampling or export-only-on-errors patterns.
[08:56] Marcus Lee: Any customers using 100% of traces in production?
[08:59] Ethan Zhou: Very few. Most use targeted capture plus full capture for important routes.
[09:04] [09:04] Anika Patel: Do you anonymize tokens when redacting? Like preserve token counts but mask content?
[09:09] Priya Malhotra: We can mask or hash token content while preserving lengths and token boundaries for analysis. Good for privacy-preserving debugging.
[09:18] Marcus Lee: About the UI, is there an API to fetch the same traces programmatically? We want to integrate into our incident tooling.
[09:23] Ethan Zhou: Absolutely. There's a Request Logs API; you can paginate, supply filters, and get signed URLs for exports.
[09:30] [09:30] Anika Patel: Could you show a flamechart expand?
[09:33] Ethan Zhou: Expanding now — see expanded kernel spans, GPU copy, enqueue, compute, postproc. You can hover to get the raw logs attached to a span.
[09:41] Jon Rivera: Raw logs — are they compressed?
[09:43] Ethan Zhou: Stored compressed in S3-like storage; UI decompresses on the fly.
[09:47] [09:47] Marcus Lee: On RBAC, can we limit who sees prompt text in the console?
[09:51] Lina Ortega: Yes. RBAC supports field-level permissions — you can revoke view of prompt_text for a role.
[09:56] Anika Patel: Nice.
[09:58] [09:58] Priya Malhotra: Quick pause for questions. Anything we haven't covered?
[10:02] Marcus Lee: What about cost tracking per-request so product can see token cost per feature?
[10:06] Ethan Zhou: We include token and cost estimates per request; Console has a cost explorer and per-route breakdowns.
[10:12] Anika Patel: Does that tie back to billing in the invoice?
[10:14] Priya Malhotra: Yes, you can map routes to billing codes and export usage for chargeback.
[10:19] [10:19] Jon Rivera: For troubleshooting, sometimes we want to replay a request against a different model variant. Do you support replay?
[10:24] Ethan Zhou: There's a Replay feature: you can re-run a historical request against another model or config in a sandbox without affecting production metrics. It logs the replay and provides diff of outputs.
[10:34] Marcus Lee: If the replay is run on hosted, are we exposing the original prompt again?
[10:38] Priya Malhotra: Replays respect the same data-retention and redaction policies — you can opt to replay with a scrubbed prompt.
[10:44] [10:44] Anika Patel: For the POC we want to capture 100% of errors and 1% of successes for the /summarize route, keep 90 days of traces, and push exports to our S3. Is that doable?
[10:53] Ethan Zhou: Yes — that's a typical POC setup. We'll size the storage and cost impact and provide recommendations.
[10:58] Priya Malhotra: Next steps recap: Priya will send tracing deck and short vid; Ethan will run a sample export and attach schema; Marcus to share compliance contact. We'll schedule POC scoping.
[11:10] Marcus Lee: Sounds good. A couple of quick real questions: Any gotchas with GDPR when exporting to US buckets?
[11:15] Lina Ortega: You can choose region for storage; for Hosted we store per-region by default. For cross-border you need lawful basis or anonymization. We'll share legal guidance.
[11:25] Anika Patel: One more — what if we hit a rare edge case where trace grouping mislabels root cause?
[11:30] Ethan Zhou: You can re-tag grouped clusters and feed that back; we use those labels to improve clustering heuristics.
[11:36] [11:36] Jon Rivera: Thanks, that helps.
[11:38] Priya Malhotra: Great. We'll follow up with the artifacts. Appreciate your time.
[11:42] Marcus Lee: Thanks everyone.
[11:44] [11:44] End of recording.
